detail: `.use(Analytics(), scoped)` passes options the codemod cannot read, and `lazy` in them decides whether the first argument is a plugin or a loader — write `.use(nextPlugin(…))` or `.use(nextPluginLazy(…))` by hand
`.use(async () => Metrics(), { lazy: isLazy })` decides `lazy` at runtime, and the 0.5 surface decides it by installer — write `.use(nextPlugin(…))` or `.use(nextPluginLazy(…))` by hand
`.use(Metrics(), { ...scoped, })` has a spread or computed member in its options, which may carry `lazy` — write the installer by hand
`.useClient(Metrics(), { runtime: "server", })` passes `runtime` to a delegate that fixed it — decide which wins and write `.use(nextPlugin(…, { … }))` by hand
`.use(...plugins)` is not the one-plugin, one-options shape the scoped queue took — write `.use(nextPlugin(plugin, { … }))` by hand, one call per plugin
`.use(wrapMetrics())` reads as an installer by its lowercase name and is left as written — if `wrapMetrics()` returns a PLUGIN rather than an installer, wrap it as `.use(nextPlugin(wrapMetrics(…)))`
